meta.title: IMRC festival & holiday calendar
meta.location: Washington, D.C., United States (Drik Panchang geoname-id 4140963)
meta.locationNote: Hindu and Jain dates follow the panchang for Washington, D.C. Tithis change at local sunrise, so a date can differ by a day in other North American cities or in India. Check your own city on drikpanchang.com before planning an event.
meta.rangeNote: Festivals, Jain observances and Rajasthan events cover November 2026 through December 2027. U.S. federal holidays cover all of 2026 and 2027.

events.name: Dhanteras
events.description: First day of Diwali. Families buy new utensils or gold and light a lamp for Dhanvantari and Lakshmi.

events.name: Roop Chaudas (Narak Chaturdashi)
events.description: Second day of Diwali, known in Marwari homes as Roop Chaudas: an early bath, ubtan and small lamps at dusk.

events.name: Diwali · Lakshmi Puja
events.description: The festival of lights. Evening Lakshmi Puja, new account books (bahi-khata) for business families, diyas and sweets.

events.name: Mahavir Nirvan Divas (Jain Diwali)
events.description: Bhagwan Mahavir attained nirvana on Diwali night; Jains light lamps and offer nirvan laddu.
events.note: Drik Panchang's Washington, DC Jain calendar lists Lakshmi Puja on this date but no separate Nirvan entry. Confirm with your derasar or Jain centre.

events.name: Govardhan Puja · Annakut
events.description: Day after Diwali. Annakut offerings of many dishes to Shri Krishna; Ram-Ram visits between families.

events.name: Bhai Dooj
events.description: Sisters apply tilak and pray for their brothers' well-being; brothers visit with gifts.

events.name: Veterans Day
events.description: U.S. federal holiday. Federal offices, banks and many schools are closed.

events.name: Gyan Panchami (Labh Panchami)
events.description: Day of reverence for knowledge and scriptures; many businesses reopen after Diwali.

events.name: Pushkar Fair (Pushkar Mela)
events.description: One of the world's largest camel and livestock fairs, with folk music, turban-tying and moustache contests by Pushkar Lake.
events.note: Rajasthan Tourism's main programme. Livestock trading starts around November 10.

events.name: Dev Uthani Ekadashi
events.description: Lord Vishnu wakes from his four-month rest; the wedding season traditionally begins.

events.name: Tulsi Vivah
events.description: Ceremonial marriage of the tulsi plant to Shaligram (Vishnu), celebrated at home and in temples.

events.name: Kartik Purnima
events.description: Full moon of Kartik: holy dips, deep-daan and the peak day of the Pushkar fair.

events.name: Thanksgiving Day
events.description: U.S. federal holiday. Federal offices, banks and many schools are closed.

events.name: Gita Jayanti · Mokshada Ekadashi
events.description: Marks the day the Bhagavad Gita was spoken; Gita path and study circles.

events.name: Christmas Day
events.description: U.S. federal holiday. Federal offices, banks and many schools are closed.

events.name: New Year's Day
events.description: U.S. federal holiday. Federal offices, banks and many schools are closed.

events.name: Makar Sankranti
events.description: Sun enters Capricorn. Kite flying across Rajasthan, til-gud sweets, and daan (giving).

events.name: Birthday of Martin Luther King, Jr.
events.description: U.S. federal holiday. Federal offices, banks and many schools are closed.

events.name: Republic Day (India)
events.description: Marks the Constitution of India coming into force in 1950.

events.name: Vasant Panchami
events.description: Welcomes spring and honours Saraswati, goddess of learning; yellow clothes and sweets.

events.name: Nagaur Fair (Ramdeoji Cattle Fair)
events.description: Marwar's great cattle fair in Nagaur: Nagori bullocks, camel races and folk performances.
events.note: From Rajasthan Tourism's 2024–2030 forecast list. Final dates are announced closer to the event.

events.name: Washington's Birthday (Presidents' Day)
events.description: U.S. federal holiday. Federal offices, banks and many schools are closed.

events.name: Desert Festival, Jaisalmer
events.description: Three days of folk culture on the Thar dunes near Jaisalmer: camel polo, Mr Desert, puppeteers and Kalbelia dancers.
events.note: From Rajasthan Tourism's 2024–2030 forecast list. Final dates are announced closer to the event.

events.name: Maha Shivaratri
events.description: Night of Shiva: fasting, night-long worship and abhishek at temples.

events.name: Holika Dahan
events.description: Bonfire on the full-moon night before Holi; Gangaur worship begins the next morning for many Marwari women.

events.name: Holi (Dhulandi)
events.description: Festival of colours, gulal and gujiya; the 16–18 day Gangaur puja starts from this day.

events.name: Sheetla Ashtami (Basoda)
events.description: Worship of Sheetla Mata; families eat food cooked the day before (basoda). Widely kept in Rajasthan.

events.name: Chaitra Navratri · Nav Samvat begins
events.description: Hindu new year (Vikram Samvat 2084) and the start of nine nights of Durga worship.
events.note: Ends with Ram Navami on April 14.

events.name: Gangaur
events.description: Rajasthan's beloved festival of Gauri (Parvati) and Isar (Shiva). Women and girls who began puja after Holi dress Gangaur, sing songs, and lead processions.

events.name: Ram Navami
events.description: Birth of Shri Ram, closing Chaitra Navratri.

events.name: Mahavir Jayanti
events.description: Birth of Bhagwan Mahavir, the 24th Tirthankara: processions, abhishek and charity.
events.note: India observes it on April 19, 2027; Washington, DC falls a day earlier.

events.name: Hanuman Jayanti
events.description: Birth of Hanuman; Hanuman Chalisa recitation and temple visits (including Salasar Balaji devotees).

events.name: Akshaya Tritiya (Aakha Teej)
events.description: An auspicious day for new beginnings. In Marwar it is Aakha Teej, with khichda and many weddings.

events.name: Memorial Day
events.description: U.S. federal holiday. Federal offices, banks and many schools are closed.

events.name: Juneteenth National Independence Day (observed)
events.description: U.S. federal holiday. Federal offices, banks and many schools are closed.

events.name: Independence Day (observed)
events.description: U.S. federal holiday. Federal offices, banks and many schools are closed.

events.name: Guru Purnima
events.description: Honours teachers and gurus.

events.name: Hariyali Teej (Sawan Teej)
events.description: Monsoon festival for women: green clothes, mehendi, swings and ghewar.

events.name: Independence Day (India)
events.description: India's independence in 1947; flag hoisting and community gatherings across North America.

events.name: Raksha Bandhan
events.description: Sisters tie rakhi on their brothers' wrists.

events.name: Kajari Teej (Badi Teej · Satudi Teej)
events.hindi: कजरी तीज · बड़ी तीज · सातुड़ी तीज
events.description: A major Marwari women's fast. Satu (sattu) sweets, neemdi mata puja, and the fast is broken after seeing the moon.

events.name: Krishna Janmashtami
events.description: Birth of Shri Krishna at midnight; fasting, bhajans and jhanki decorations.

events.name: Paryushan Parva (Shvetambar)
events.description: Eight days of fasting, study and reflection, ending with Samvatsari.

events.name: Ganesh Chaturthi
events.description: Welcomes Ganesh, remover of obstacles; ten days of worship to Anant Chaturdashi.
events.note: Ganesh Visarjan / Anant Chaturdashi on September 14.

events.name: Samvatsari · Michhami Dukkadam
events.description: Final day of Paryushan: pratikraman and asking forgiveness of every living being.

events.name: Labor Day
events.description: U.S. federal holiday. Federal offices, banks and many schools are closed.

events.name: Pitru Paksha (Shraadh)
events.description: Fortnight for remembering ancestors with tarpan and food offerings.
events.note: Ends on Sarva Pitru Amavasya, September 29.

events.name: Sharad Navratri
events.description: Nine nights of Durga worship, garba and dandiya.
events.note: Durga Ashtami October 7; Maha Navami October 8.

events.name: Gandhi Jayanti
events.description: Birthday of Mahatma Gandhi; a national holiday and International Day of Non-Violence.

events.name: Dussehra (Vijayadashami)
events.description: Victory of good over evil; Ravan dahan and Shami puja.

events.name: Columbus Day
events.description: U.S. federal holiday. Federal offices, banks and many schools are closed.

events.name: Marwar Festival, Jodhpur
events.description: Jodhpur's festival of Marwar folk music (Maand) and heroes, at Mehrangarh, Umaid Stadium and the Osian dunes.
events.note: From Rajasthan Tourism's 2024–2030 forecast list. The 2026 edition ran Oct 24–25.

events.name: Sharad Purnima
events.description: Harvest full moon; kheer kept in the moonlight. The Marwar Festival in Jodhpur is timed to it.

events.name: Karva Chauth
events.description: Married women fast from sunrise to moonrise for their husbands' long life.

events.name: Dhanteras
events.description: First day of Diwali. Families buy new utensils or gold and light a lamp for Dhanvantari and Lakshmi.

events.name: Diwali · Lakshmi Puja
events.description: The festival of lights. Evening Lakshmi Puja, new account books (bahi-khata), diyas and sweets.
events.note: India's government calendar lists Diwali on Oct 29, 2027; in Washington, DC it falls on Oct 28.

events.name: Roop Chaudas (Narak Chaturdashi)
events.description: Second day of Diwali. In 2027 the Washington, DC panchang lists it on the same day as Lakshmi Puja.
events.note: Drik Panchang lists Kali Chaudas on Oct 27 and Narak Chaturdashi on Oct 28 for Washington, DC.

events.name: Mahavir Nirvan Divas (Jain Diwali)
events.description: Bhagwan Mahavir attained nirvana on Diwali night; Jains light lamps and offer nirvan laddu.
events.note: Shown on Diwali night for Washington, DC; Indian Jain calendars list Oct 29. Confirm with your derasar or Jain centre.

events.name: Govardhan Puja · Annakut
events.description: Day after Diwali. Annakut offerings to Shri Krishna; Ram-Ram visits between families.

events.name: Bhai Dooj
events.description: Sisters apply tilak and pray for their brothers' well-being.

events.name: Gyan Panchami (Labh Panchami)
events.description: Day of reverence for knowledge and scriptures.

events.name: Pushkar Fair (Pushkar Mela)
events.description: Camel and livestock fair with cultural programmes, ending on Kartik Purnima.
events.note: From Rajasthan Tourism's 2024–2030 forecast list. Final dates are announced closer to the event.

events.name: Dev Uthani Ekadashi
events.description: Lord Vishnu wakes from his four-month rest; the wedding season begins.

events.name: Kartik Purnima
events.description: Full moon of Kartik: holy dips and deep-daan.

events.name: Thanksgiving Day

events.name: Gita Jayanti · Mokshada Ekadashi
events.description: Marks the day the Bhagavad Gita was spoken.

events.description: U.S. federal holiday. Federal offices, banks and many schools are closed.
events.note: January 1, 2028 is a Saturday; OPM lists Friday, December 31, 2027.
